events.summary:
Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week

Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.

After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. A global outage of vital Microsoft systems has crippled businesses and public services around the world. The tech company said it was seeing “early signs of stabilisation” after the failure affected millions of users for more than 12 hours on Thursday and Friday.

Some but not all users were reporting problems with services including Microsoft Teams and Outlook email. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Copilot, Microsoft’s AI chatbot, according to the company. Microsoft said that there were no indications that the outage had been caused by a cyber-attack. We are covering the recovery efforts and continuing impact in this live blog.

Who are the main people involved? For more information on the cast of characters, Dan Milmo has this profile of outgoing Huang, who went from washing dishes at Denny’s to becoming the rock star of AI, and Dara Kerr has this piece answering the question: who is Colette Kress? events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
events.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

events.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
events.summary: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

events.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
events.summary: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

events.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
events.summary: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

events.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
events.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
events.summary: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
events.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
events.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

events.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
events.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

events.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
events.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
events.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
events.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

events.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
events.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

events.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
events.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

events.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
events.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

events.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
events.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

events.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
events.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

events.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
events.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

events.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
events.summary: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

events.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
events.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
events.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
events.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

events.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
events.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

events.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
events.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

events.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
events.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

events.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
events.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

events.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
events.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

events.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
events.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

events.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
events.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

events.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
events.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

events.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
events.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

events.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
events.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

events.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
events.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

events.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
events.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

events.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
events.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

events.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
events.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

events.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
events.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

events.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
events.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

events.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
events.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

events.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
events.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

events.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
events.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

events.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
events.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

events.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
events.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

events.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
events.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

events.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
events.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

events.title: The Nvidia affair: Are markets about to fall out of love with AI?
events.summary: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia exposes the vulnerabilities behind the AI boom. As equities reel in response to his resignation following extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage and a summons to testify before US lawmakers, questions mount over who is really in charge of tech and whether the immense capital riding on it can survive the turmoil.

events.title: November 13 Paris attacks: Eleven years later, France pays tribute to victims
events.summary: Eleven years on, France pays tribute to the victims of the November 13 attacks. French officials, victims’ associations and families gathered this Friday to pay their respects to those killed in the attacks in Paris on November 13, 2015.

events.title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
events.summary: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

events.title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
events.summary: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area.  Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.

events.title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
events.summary: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.

events.title: West Bank: ‘Without international trade and financial support, large settlements would not exist’
events.summary: France is considering legislation to restrict trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories, namely the West Bank. Ivar Ekeland, Professor Emeritus at Paris Dauphine-PSL University and Chair of the Organization of Academics for the Respect of International Law in Palestine, discusses the proposed measures with Alison Sargent. He calls for restrictions to cover n ot only goods but also services, including financial services, insurance and tourism. "Without the support of financial entities, of insurance, of providing goods and so on, settlements, big settlements, would not exist," he argues.

events.title: UN refugee chief Barham Salih slams 'shameful' war in Sudan, urges 'political solution'
events.summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, UN refugee chief Barham Salih called the war in Sudan "shameful" and urged the world to end it. With forced displacement at a record high, he warned that funding cuts are hurting people "in dire need". "Efficiency has its limits," he said. Salih also defended the "integrity of the asylum system".

events.title: France asks Brussels to examine Algeria's non-compliance of EU association agreement
events.summary: France announced on Friday that it will ask the European Commission to "examine" Algeria's non-compliance with its EU association agreement. Earlier in July, Algiers imposed a near-blanket ban on French imports, and last month, Algeria suspended urea shipments to France.

events.title: Nvidia scandal: How close was ex-CEO to Trump?
events.summary: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Just how close Huang was to Trump and the extent of the influence tech giants have on his administration are some of the questions that still need answering, says France 24’s Douglas Herbert.

events.title: Russia strikes targets across Ukraine as Kyiv launches nearly 1,200 drones
events.summary: Russian strikes hit targets across Ukraine on Thursday, with one attack damaging a hospital. Ukraine meanwhile fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.

events.title: Haitian forces recapture national stadium after two years of gang control
events.summary: Haitian security forces regained control Thursday, November 12, of the country's main stadium that had been under gang control for two years, forcing the national football team to play elsewhere. The Haitian National Police said in a statement that it had taken "full control" of the venue with the Task Force, a private security group serving the government, after which it left the stadium under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers.

events.title: Roger Waters launches heartfelt plea for 'an end to the genocide in Gaza'
events.summary: Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters has always mixed art with activism. A long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause, the star guitarist has now released a re-imagined version of the rock anthem "Comfortably Numb" with Palestinian American singer Mona Miari singing in Arabic. He tells FRANCE 24's Lyana Saleh why proceeds of the record are going to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund and why he can never become "Comfortably Numb" with the violence and suffering in Gaza.

events.title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
events.summary: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".

events.title: The truth about Douma: How Syria covered up a chemical attack
events.summary: On April 7, 2018, the Syrian town of Douma, on the outskirts of the capital Damascus, was targeted by a chemical attack. Evidence pointed to the Syrian regime, yet proof vanished, and eyewitnesses went silent. Eight years later, FRANCE 24's Jenna Le Bras tracked down survivors and witnesses of the deadly attack. She also met representatives of some of the world's most powerful institutions to understand how a massive cover-up campaign had been orchestrated by the regime, with Russian support.

events.title: What does the 'Blue Tsunami' mean for US media?
events.summary: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop looks at the impact of the midterm elections in the United States. While the results are being reckoned with by Republicans and celebrated by Democrats, what does it all mean for the press? Some media analysts wonder whether certain outlets, particularly ones accused of being cosy with the Trump administration, will change their tone. Our guest this week is International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert.

events.title: Most Ukrainians 'think there's no chance of a peace deal' with Russia
events.summary: Ukrainian attacks killed at least nine people in Russia overnight, while Moscow struck a hospital in Kyiv and killed at least three in the south of the country, officials on both sides said Friday. It comes a day after intense shuttle diplomacy in US-led talks to end the war approaching its fifth year but, says France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg, most people in Ukraine think there is "no chance" of a peace deal being reached.

events.title: 'A lot of emotion' as Paris marks 11 years since terror attacks
events.summary: France on Friday marked 11 years since the November 13, 2015, terror attacks that left more than 130 dead in the capital. France 24's James André reports from outside the Bataclan concert venue, one of the sites targeted in the attacks, where he says there was "a lot of emotion" as homage was paid to the victims.

events.title: 🔴 Live: Microsoft reports 'improvements' to Outlook services in North America, Europe
UK rocked by comedians' sex scandals
events.summary: The UK is facing a reckoning in the world of entertainment, as two well-known comedy figures find themselves at the centre of serious allegations and headlines. This as Russell Brand is jailed for more than 10 years after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault and David Walliams faces serious allegations of sexual misconduct.

events.title: The scourge of femicide in Mexico: Impunity reigns in state of Morelos
events.summary: When Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president in 2024, she pledged to tackle violence against women. And while femicides have fallen since she took office, the numbers remain alarming, with around 520 murders so far this year. In the small state of Morelos, just outside the capital Mexico City, four female students have been murdered since January, including a Spanish woman on an exchange programme. The state has one of the highest femicide rates in the country.

events.title: Ukraine’s mobilisation methods spark criticism
events.summary: Social media in Ukraine is full of videos showing suspected cases of forced mobilisation. Such incidents are known as “busification”, as the recruitment officers typically take the conscripts away in minibuses. The videos have been fuelling growing opposition to the recruitment practices.

events.title: Nvidia scandal: Was Alice Huang really a Chinese spy?
events.summary: It is another twist in the downfall of Jensen Huang, CEO of AI chip giant Nvidia, who resigned on Thursday. The US Justice Department says it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman he had an affair with, was a spy. CNN is also reporting sources from across the US intelligence community who say there is no definitive proof she was an intelligence asset for Beijing

events.title: It's 'game over' for Jensen Huang, king of AI chips
events.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, November 13: We look at reactions to the resignation of Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia. It comes in the wake of multiple affairs he allegedly had, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. What are the repercussions for the AI industry and for AI trade relations? Also: France's Les Bleus lose to Italy in the Nations League, marking Zinédine Zidane's first defeat as coach. Plus: a raccoon that went viral for getting drunk last year ends up raising a lot of money for an animal shelter!

events.title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
events.summary: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium on Thursday, ending two years of gang control. Salvadoran troops have now taken over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush in which four of its troops went missing.

events.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

events.summary: The Rubik's Cube, invented by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik in 1974, has become one of the world's most beloved puzzles

events.summary: Officials say a passenger van veered off a mountainous road and plunged into a river in northern Pakistan, killing 11 people and injuring three others

events.summary: Spain’s interim lower house of parliament has ratified housing measures designed to limit evictions and real estate speculation

events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's image in his birthplace, Taiwan, has been tainted after the FBI began investigating his affair with an alleged Chinese agent

events.title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

events.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
events.summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.

events.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
events.summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.

events.title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
events.summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

events.title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
events.summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

events.title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.

events.title: Clashes erupt in France as ‘Black Thursday’ protests sweep the nation
events.summary: “Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”

events.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
events.summary: Six women alleged that the British comedian had sexually assaulted them at his home, in hotels and public bathrooms. Brand has denied all claims.

events.title: Melania Trump calls for ‘enduring’ Russia-Ukraine peace as she hosts top officials at the White House
events.summary: Ukraine has been reeling from the worst collapse in relations with Washington since the start of the war.

events.title: U.S. Marine dies in Japan during training, military says
events.summary: The person, who has yet to be named, died Tuesday in Okinawa, the 3rd Marine Division said.

events.title: U.S. will stop $4B in aid to Israel at the end of the year, Trump says
events.summary: Oil prices slid in response to the deal, which the president said was Netanyahu’s idea.
